sentence: First-time mothers are offered at least 10 antenatal appointments and 2 ultrasound scans; those who have given birth before are offered at least 7 appointments.
The booking appointment with a midwife is usually the first, and NICE recommends offering it by about 10 weeks of pregnancy.
Screening tests are optional, and NICE says a woman can accept or decline any part of any screening programme.
Exact schedules vary between local maternity services.
The NHS says first-time mothers are offered at least 10 appointments and 2 ultrasound scans.
Those who have given birth before are offered at least 7 appointments.
The exact schedule varies between local maternity services.
The booking appointment is usually the first appointment with a midwife and can take around an hour.
NHS guidance says it is best to attend as early as possible, and NICE recommends offering it by about 10 weeks of pregnancy.
At this appointment, NICE recommends that staff discuss and offer screening for infectious diseases (HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B), sickle cell disease and thalassaemia, and fetal anomalies.
Later appointments happen at intervals through pregnancy, and the midwife checks blood pressure, urine, bump size and the baby's movements.
The 11 to 14 week scan estimates the due date, checks development and shows whether there is more than one baby; it is sometimes called the dating scan.
The 18 to 21 week scan, often called the anomaly or 20-week scan, checks development and screens for rare conditions.
Screening for Down's, Edwards' and Patau's syndromes is offered at the dating scan, and it is the woman's choice whether to have it.
NICE says the woman can accept or decline any part of any of the screening programmes offered.
The free flu vaccine is offered in every pregnancy, as is the whooping cough vaccine.
